tactics.name: State Institution Obstruction
tactics.question: Did state institutions (ministries, regulators, legislators) act in ways that obstruct tobacco control policy?
tactics.hint: State Institution Obstruction — look for: delayed regulations, weakened amendments, captured agencies

tactics.name: Media / Information Obstruction
tactics.question: Did media or information channels promote industry-favourable framing, spread disinformation, or suppress evidence?
tactics.hint: Media / Information Obstruction — look for: industry-funded studies cited, policy-discrediting narratives

tactics.name: Civil-Society Institution Obstruction
tactics.question: Did civil-society bodies (NGOs, academic groups, professional associations) obstruct or water down this tobacco policy?
tactics.hint: Civil-Society Institution Obstruction — look for: front groups posing as civil society, captured NGOs

tactics.name: Legal / Litigation Obstruction
tactics.question: Did the industry or its allies use legal threats, lawsuits, or constitutional challenges to obstruct the policy?
tactics.hint: Legal / Litigation Obstruction — look for: suing the government, threatening trade disputes, intellectual property claims

tactics.name: Financial / Economic Obstruction
tactics.question: Did the industry exaggerate their economic importance or threaten job losses to block the policy?
tactics.hint: Financial / Economic Obstruction — look for: claims of massive job losses, economic ruin, threats to close factories

tactics.name: Political / Legislative Obstruction
tactics.question: Did the industry maneuver to hijack the political and legislative process directly?
tactics.hint: Political / Legislative Obstruction — look for: aggressive lobbying, campaign contributions, drafting alternative weak laws

tactics.name: Smuggling / Illicit Trade Exaggeration
tactics.question: Did the industry exaggerate the threat of smuggling and illicit trade to oppose tax or packaging policies?
tactics.hint: Smuggling / Illicit Trade — look for: claims that taxes will increase the black market, funding illicit trade reports

tactics.name: Public Relations / CSR
tactics.question: Did the industry use Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives to buy goodwill and distract from the policy?
tactics.hint: Public Relations / CSR — look for: funding youth programs, environmental cleanups, or COVID-19 relief donations

tactics.name: Scientific Disinformation
tactics.question: Did the industry fabricate or fund biased scientific research to discredit proven tobacco control science?
tactics.hint: Scientific Disinformation — look for: funding dubious scientists, creating fake institutes, undermining peer-reviewed data

tactics.name: Tax / Pricing Obstruction
tactics.question: Did the industry manipulate pricing structures or oppose tax harmonization to keep products affordable?
tactics.hint: Tax / Pricing Obstruction — look for: absorbing tax hikes, creating cheaper sub-brands, opposing uniform excise taxes

tactics.name: Harm Reduction Obstruction
tactics.question: Did the industry aggressively push novel products (e-cigarettes, HTPs) under the guise of harm reduction to bypass bans?
tactics.hint: Harm Reduction Obstruction — look for: claiming e-cigarettes are safe, opposing novel product bans, marketing to youth

tactics.name: Inter-Governmental Organization Obstruction
tactics.question: Did the industry use international trade agreements (WTO, bilateral treaties) to intimidate the government?
tactics.hint: Inter-Governmental Organization Obstruction — look for: invoking WTO rules, claiming violation of free trade agreements

tactics.name: Front Group Involvement
tactics.question: Did the industry fund astroturf organizations (fake grassroots) or front groups to simulate public opposition?
tactics.hint: Front Group Involvement — look for: smokers' rights groups, retailer associations, or think tanks funded by big tobacco
